correctness.rationale: The final claim concerns the bounded continuous lacunary trace F(x)=sum_{j>=1}2^{-j}sin(2^j x_1) on R^{n-1}, n>=3, and its hyperbolic Poisson extension U on the CLOSED Euclidean upper half-space. Independently reconstruct the proof: for 0<r<1/2 choose J=floor(log_2(1/r)), so 2^{-(J+1)}<r<=2^{-J}. At any horizontal increment of length <=r, each term differs by at most min(r,2^{1-j}); thus omega_F(r)<=Jr+2^{1-J}<=Jr+4r. At x=0,h=re_1, the first J normalized summands equal sin(2^jr)/(2^jr)=1+O((2^jr)^2). The total quadratic error r^2 sum_{j<=J}4^j=O(1), and the normalized tail has magnitude <=2^{-J}/r<2. Therefore F(re_1)/r=J+O(1), giving omega_F(r)=r log(1/r)/log(2)+O(r) for ALL sufficiently small radii, not only dyadic ones. For U=P_y*F, the nonnegative unit-mass kernel gives horizontal contraction |U(x+h,y)-U(x,y)|<=omega_F(|h|), and the primary source proves sup_{x,y}|d_y U|<=C_d. Splitting an arbitrary Euclidean increment of length <=r into horizontal and vertical increments gives omega_U(r)<=omega_F(r)+C_dr. Boundary continuity and admissible boundary pairs give omega_U(r)>=omega_F(r). Both limits are 1/log(2). The constant is dimension-independent only for this fixed normalization; no universal theorem is asserted. Verified the source package six files from actual pinned Git blob IDs and reconstructed its Git tree hash; the analytic bound needs no finite experiment.

value.rationale: Modest but motivated narrow exact invariant. The fixed lacunary sine series is not an arbitrary parameter slice: it is the canonical explicit obstruction in the 2026 hyperbolic endpoint theorem and a classical critical Weierstrass object. Its natural first-difference modulus quantifies the precise borderline between global Euclidean Lipschitz regularity and the critical Zygmund log-Lipschitz scale. The exact normalized coefficient 1/log(2), proved at every radius rather than merely a dyadic test sequence, is not supplied by the predecessor weak-order statements. A full-extension transfer proves that no extra leading logarithmic loss arises from the hyperbolic Poisson layer in any n>=3. A future comparison of sharp endpoint moduli for other kernels or counterexamples can use this explicit calibrated coefficient. The value is limited: an elementary dyadic split suffices, and there is no new class-level endpoint theorem, phase diagram, or second-order expansion. This limit is accepted as a natural exact test-example fact, not as a broad breakthrough or paper-sized result.
